claim_5_text: The system of claim 1, further comprising at least two transducers positioned on or about the catheter, wherein at least one transducer is a pressure sensor and at least one transducer is a flow sensor.

L1.passage: at least one transducer is a pressure sensor
L1.rationale: Claim 5 explicitly discloses a pressure sensor on a catheter in the CSF space

L2.rationale: No mention of venous sinus. The catheter accesses CSF space, not venous sinus. No venous pressure measurement.

L3.limitation: differential is calculated from the two
L3.rationale: No differential calculation. Two sensors exist (pressure + flow) but no differential between CSF and venous pressure is computed.

L4.limitation: measurements obtained in eShunt anatomical context (subarachnoid to dural venous sinus)
L4.rationale: Catheter accesses CSF space but NOT via endovascular approach to dural venous sinus. No subarachnoid-to-venous shunt context.

L5.limitation: differential used to detect/predict obstruction or patency failure
L5.rationale: No occlusion prediction. No patency detection. Sensors exist but output is not used for predictive monitoring.

L6.limitation: resulting signal produces a technical monitoring output
L6.passage: at least one transducer is a pressure sensor and at least one transducer is a flow sensor
L6.rationale: Transducers produce signals, but the claim does not describe monitoring output or predictive use of the signals.

rationale: US20160051801A1 discloses L1 (CSF pressure sensor) and partially L6 (transducer output). But L2 (venous sinus pressure), L3 (differential), L4 (eShunt context), and L5 (occlusion prediction) are NOT DISCLOSED. No single reference anticipates all 6 limitations.
